column2:
Create a communication SOP that defines how I (and my team, if applicable) handle all communication in my business.
My current situation: [describe — e.g., "I'm drowning in email, Slack, and DMs. Clients email me at all hours. I have no system."]
The SOP should cover: (1) Communication channels — which channel for what purpose (email for X, Slack for Y, project management tool for Z), (2) Response time expectations — by channel and by sender type (clients, prospects, team, vendors), (3) Email management system — how to triage inbox (suggest categories/labels), when to process email (time-blocking recommendations), templates for common responses, (4) Client communication norms — how often, through what channel, who handles what, (5) Internal communication norms (if team) — daily standups, weekly updates, async vs. sync rules, (6) Boundaries — out-of-hours policy, weekend policy, urgent vs. not-urgent definitions. This should save me at least 5 hours per week.

I'm a solopreneur running [your business] and I'm maxed out on time. I currently do everything myself. Here's how I spend a typical week:
[List your weekly tasks and approximate hours — e.g., "client work: 20 hours, email: 5 hours, social media: 4 hours, bookkeeping: 2 hours, admin: 3 hours, sales calls: 4 hours, content creation: 6 hours"]
My hourly rate / what my time is worth: [your rate or what you charge clients per hour].
Analyze my week and tell me: (1) Which tasks to delegate first (using the "low skill, high time" framework), (2) What type of person to hire for each (VA, specialist, agency), (3) Expected cost for each delegation (hourly rates for [your country or remote]), (4) ROI analysis — how much time I'll free up vs. how much I'll spend, (5) What I should NEVER delegate (my highest-value activities), (6) A phased delegation plan — what to outsource first, second, third, as revenue allows. Goal: get me to only doing the $200+/hour work.
